newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU delay would cost masses of jobs - CDU labour wing.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay would cost masses of jobs - CDU labour wing.

text.p: The head of the labour wing of the ruling Christian Democratic Union (CDU) said on Friday that a delayed start for European monetary union would cost masses of jobs.
Hermann-Josef Arentz said a delay would cause an appreciation of the mark that would boost imports and blunt Germany's export boom.
"The two together would cost masses of jobs," he said in a radio interview. "It would be the worst thing that could happen to the labour market."
European leaders will decide in about one year what nations qualify to participate in the economic and monetary union (EMU) from its start in January 1999, basing on their 1997 economic performance.

The difficulties faced by key countries such as Germany and France in whipping their economies into shape for EMU have fuelled speculation that a delay was on the cards, despite repeated top-level assurances to the contrary.
Arentz said countries with stable currencies and low levels of debt -- requirements for participation in EMU -- are in a better position to help their labour markets over the long term.
Calls for a Europe-wide labour policy "make some sense," but the discussion should be separate from the EMU issue, Arentz said.
"Labour market policy is a challenge that must be met in Europe with support for the individual nations. Monetary union must also be a social union," he said.
